lesson_title: Same Farm, Same Workers, Double the Harvest
hook_text: Same land. Same two workers. Twice the maize. And the soil is getting better, not worse. How?
clip_script: Year one: two tonnes of maize per hectare. Then training, better seed and drip irrigation. Year three: four tonnes, same land, same workers. That is productivity: more output from the same inputs. When lots of farms and businesses do this, the whole country produces more. That is economic growth. But next door, a farmer pumped the river dry and ploughed to the bank. Two good years, then the soil washed away. Unsustainable. Mama Dube rotates crops, mulches the soil and runs a solar pump. Productive today, fertile for her grandchildren. Grow more, and grow it so it lasts.
visual_style: A whiteboard split field: one side with drip lines, beans, mulch and a solar panel thriving; the other side with a dry river and eroded gullies.
mood: Hopeful and smart, with a cautionary twist.
pacing: Quick before-and-after numbers, a neighbour contrast, then a calm sustainable close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and spot one way your school could use water or electricity more sustainably.
